title: Vector goldset offline evaluation harness and drift alerting
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a reproducible offline evaluation harness for Redwood embeddings and reranking flows that exercises: curated golden-case queries and expected vectors, bulk offline metrics (MRR, Recall@K, NDCG, cosine/inner-product distributions), sensitivity to quantization/approximate index settings, and drift detection pipelines with automated alerting. The goal is to give product and infra teams fast feedback when a model change, quantization profile, or indexing config causes a regression in user-visible relevance or a silent drift in vector space. The harness must scale to multi-million example corpora in benchmarking mode and support fast nightly/continuous checks against sampled production traffic for drift monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Daily CI job runs: golden-case suite executes and writes results to metrics store (datapoints, histograms)
Baseline metrics recorded for current production model and quantization settings in metrics backend
Drift detector produces alerts when thresholds crossed (configurable by cohort) and raises a Slack/GitHub incident ticket
Performance benchmark: offline evaluation can re-run a 2M-document recall sweep within a 6-hour window on Dedicated test pool
Integrations: Grafana dashboard and Console panel populated with historical metrics and example failing queries
Runbook: triage playbook and remediation steps documented in Confluence linked from alert notifications
steps: Define goldset selection criteria and format. Create 3 cohorts: core-queries (high-value), long-tail (edge cases), and synthetics (adversarial)
Implement ingestion pipeline: normalize inputs, store embeddings and metadata in S3 (parquet) and snapshot reference indices (FAISS / Annoy)
Build offline runner: kNN recall, reranker emulation, metric calculators (MRR, Recall@K, NDCG, cosine-distribution summaries)
Add quantization/FAISS config matrix runner to measure sensitivity across configs
Create nightly scheduler for sampled production traffic checks (sampling window, downsample policy)
Implement drift detection logic (population shift, embedding centroid drift, metric delta thresholds) and rule-based alerting
Wire metrics into Prometheus/Grafana and instrument Console with per-run artifacts and example hard failures
Add CI gating for embedding changes: optional step to block runtime rollout on severe regressions
notes: Trade-off: heavy offline runs are useful for coverage but expensive; we will keep daily smoke runs for critical cohorts and weekly full-bench jobs for cost reasons
Decision: use FAISS for local benchmarking to approximate production ANN, but keep an abstraction layer so we can plug in open-source vector DBs or Redwood indexing later
Review feedback (2026-02-25): PM asked for per-customer cohort capability; will add customer_id tag support to goldset format in next sprint
Privacy: golden sets will exclude PII and sensitive user data; sampled production windows will run in a dedicated VPC with data retention policy
Scale note: initial benchmark target is 2M documents; if customers request larger numbers, follow-up ticket will expand to 20M+ with sharded index runners
